# Visualizando el modelo discriminante Gaussiano

Consideraremos varios ejemplos que nos ayudarán a visualizar el proceso del *análisis discriminante lineal* en el marco teórico del modelo discriminante Gaussiano.

## Dos grupos, una variable

Emezaremos por considerar el caso en el que tenemos dos grupos con medias
$$\mu_{1} = -2 \qquad \mu_{2} = 2$$
y varianza $\sigma^{2} = 1$. Supondremos que los priors están dados por
$$\pi_{1} = \frac{1}{3} \qquad \pi_{2} = \frac{2}{3}$$
En este caso, las funciones discriminantes están dadas por:
$$\delta_{1}(x) = -2x -\frac{4}{2} + \log(\frac{1}{3})$$
y
$$\delta_{2}(x) = 2x -\frac{4}{2} + \log(\frac{2}{3})$$
La diferencia entre estas funciones está dada por
$$\Delta_{21}(x) = \delta_{2}(x)-\delta_{1}(x) = 4x +\log(2)$$
Se sigue que la frontera de decisión está dada por
$$x = - \frac{\log(2)}{4}$$

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 15
# Load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(krulRutils)
library(patchwork)
# Parameters
mu1  <- -2
mu2  <-  2
sd   <-  1
pi1  <- 1/3
pi2  <- 2/3
x_star <- -log(2) / (2*(mu2))


# Discriminant functions (from your derivation)
delta1 <- function(x) mu1 * x - mu1^2 / 2 + log(pi1)
delta2 <- function(x) mu2 * x - mu2^2 / 2 + log(pi2)

# A reasonable x-range for plotting
x_grid <- seq(-10, 10, length.out = 400)

disc_df <- tibble(
  x      = x_grid,
  delta1 = delta1(x),
  delta2 = delta2(x)
) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(delta1, delta2),
               names_to = "Grupo",
               values_to = "Discriminante") %>%
  mutate(Grupo = recode(Grupo,
                        delta1 = "Grupo 1",
                        delta2 = "Grupo 2"))

p_discriminant <- ggplot(disc_df, aes(x = x, y = Discriminante, color = Grupo)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  c_scale_color("C blue", "C green") +
  labs(
    title = "Funciones Discriminantes",
    x     = "x",
    y     = "Discriminante",
    color = "Grupos"
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = x_star, linetype = "dashed", color = c_pal("C red"), linewidth = 1) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-6,6)) +
  theme_krul()

dens_df <- tibble(
  x   = x_grid,
  w1  = pi1 * dnorm(x, mean = mu1, sd = sd),
  w2  = pi2 * dnorm(x, mean = mu2, sd = sd)
) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(w1, w2),
               names_to = "group",
               values_to = "density") %>%
  mutate(group = recode(group,
                        w1 = "Grupo 1",
                        w2 = "Grupo 2"))

p_density <- ggplot(dens_df, aes(x = x, y = density, fill = group)) +
  geom_area(alpha = 0.4, position = "identity") +
  c_scale_fill("C blue", "C green") +
  geom_line(aes(color = group), linewidth = 1) +
  c_scale_color("C blue", "C green") +
  labs(
    title = "Funciones de densidad",
    x     = "x",
    y     = "Densidad",
    fill  = "Grupos",
    color = "Grupos"
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = x_star, linetype = "dashed", color = c_pal("C red"), linewidth = 1) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-6,6)) +
  theme_krul()

set.seed(123)  # for reproducibility

n1 <- 100
n2 <- 200

x1 <- rnorm(n1, mean = mu1, sd = sd)
x2 <- rnorm(n2, mean = mu2, sd = sd)

sample_df <- tibble(
  x     = c(x1, x2),
  group = factor(c(rep("Grupo 1", n1), rep("Grupo 2", n2)))
)

p_hist <- ggplot(sample_df, aes(x = x, fill = group)) +
  geom_histogram(
    position = "identity",
    color = "black",
    alpha    = 0.4,
    bins     = 30
  ) +
  c_scale_fill("C blue", "C green") +
  labs(
    title = "Muestras de los dos grupos",
    x     = "x",
    y     = "",
    fill  = "Grupos"
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = x_star, linetype = "dashed", color = c_pal("C red"), linewidth = 1) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-6,6)) +
  theme_krul()

p_comb <- p_density / p_discriminant/p_hist 

p_comb
```
